## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `Example`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `alfresco-example`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **Example**.

## Step 2: Open the connector palette

1. Select **+ Add Connection** button in the Connections section of the low-code canvas sidebar to open the connector search palette.

## Step 3: Search for and select the Alfresco connector

1. <!-- manual: Enter "alfresco" in the palette search box to filter the connector list. -->
2. <!-- manual: Locate the Alfresco connector card (ballerinax/alfresco) in the results. -->
3. <!-- manual: Select the connector card to open the Alfresco connection configuration form. -->

## Step 4: Bind Alfresco connection parameters to configurables

1. For each connection field, open the helper panel, navigate to the **Configurables** tab, select **+ New Configurable**, enter the variable name and type, and select **Save** to auto-inject the configurable into the field.
2. <!-- manual: enter the variable name; type -->

## Step 5: Save the Alfresco connection

1. Select **Save** to persist the connection configuration.

## Step 6: Set actual values for your configurables

1. In the left panel of WSO2 Integrator, select **Configurations** (listed at the bottom of the project tree, under Data Mappers).
2. Run the shell command `.venv/bin/python tools/write_config.py --project alfresco-example --expect alfrescoServiceUrl,alfrescoUsername,alfrescoPassword,alfrescoParentNodeId` to set the configurable values.

## Step 7: Add an automation entry point

1. In the low-code canvas, select **+ Add Entry Point** to add a new Automation entry point.
2. <!-- manual: Accept the default trigger interval or set a suitable schedule. -->
3. Select **Create** to confirm the automation and view its flow body on the canvas.
